newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria has $72 mln capital account deficit H1'96.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria has $72 mln capital account deficit H1'96.

text.p: Bulgaria posted a $71.9 million capital account deficit in the first half of this year after a $22.3 million deficit for the same period of 1995, Bulgarian National Bank's (BNB) preliminary figures showed.
This was due to a 36 percent year-on-year drop in direct foreign investments in Bulgaria and a massive resident capital outflow, the BNB said.
Direct foreign investment fell by $27.6 million from January through June year-on-year to $49 million, figures showed.
The period was also characterised by a large resident capital outflow, the BNB said.
"For the first time since 1991 when market reforms began, firms and individuals withdrew $512.4 million of foreign currency deposits in banks in six months," the BNB said in a statement.
This was due to the Bulgarian lev's depreciation against major currencies aggravated by a banking crisis, which undermined confidence in local commercial banks, the BNB said.
The lev retreated near 156 to the dollar at the end of June from around 71 at the beginning of January on the domestic interbank market.
Portfolio investments in the first half of this year ammounted to a net figure of $30.6 million as Bulgarian commercial banks' investments in foreign securities increased by $44.1 million.
Principal payments to Bulgaria on credits extended to other countries totalled $174.9 million in the first half of 1996, up from $135.9 million in the same period of last year.
Principal payments to Bulgaria's foreign lenders totalled $218.0 million, up from $152.5 million in the first half of 1995, figures showed.

The lev depreciation against foreign currencies was also the reason for a capital flight during the first half of the year despite the high BNB's main interest rate, which was gradually raised to 108 percent in May from 34 percent in January. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
